# Continual-ARC pattern note

## Two-panel occupancy intersection
When an ARC input is two equal-sized panels separated by a uniform divider row/column, and each panel is mostly a distinct nonzero background color with holes represented by 0, compare cells at identical coordinates. Output a panel of the same dimensions, placing color 2 where BOTH input panels are nonzero, and 0 wherever either panel has a hole. Evidence: task-d05f5e8a demos had same-size panels (colors 6/9 and 6/6 with zero holes), and the solved test used this cellwise overlap rule: top 1-panel AND lower 3-panel, output 2 for shared filled positions. Preserve panel orientation and alignment; remove separator from output. Do not output the union or the holes.

## Row-wise gap filling between markers
For ARC grids where a color (the marker, e.g. 3/4/6) appears at several columns within rows and the demonstrated output inserts color 2 into the horizontal gaps, preserve all original markers and fill every cell strictly between consecutive markers in that row with 2. Do this independently per row; a row with only one marker (or none) receives no fill. Example evidence: task-6e7aede8 demos had marker columns (3), (2,4), (1,5), (0,6) across successive rows, with the output filling only the intervening gaps; another demo had (1,5), (2,4), (3). Test applied: rows with columns (2,8), (1,3,7), (0,4,6), (5) become fills at 3–7; 2 and 4–6; 1–3 and 5; none. Important: never fill beyond the outermost markers or extend the row-wise pattern into adjacent rows.
